2026-12-20.title: Sunday before Yaldo
readings: Jacob's family goes down to Egypt
God's promise to the house of David
A shoot from the stump of Jesse
In your descendants all families shall be blessed
Joseph and Mary go up to Bethlehem
2026-12-20.alt: Sixth Sunday of Suboro. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was also kept as Bible Sunday. Yaldo falls on Friday 25 December.
2026-12-20.verse: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
theo: On the last Sunday before Yaldo the Church reads names: the long genealogy of Jesus, and the list of Jacob's family going down to Egypt. These lists can seem dry, but they say something essential: God's salvation enters real history, through real families, over many generations.

The prophets used the image of a tree. The royal house of David had been cut down like a stump; but Isaiah says, “A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.” Jeremiah repeats it: “I will raise up for David a righteous Branch.” When everything seemed dead, God was preparing new life from the old root.

Luke brings the promise to a dusty road. Because of a decree of Caesar Augustus, “Joseph also went from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem… He went to be registered with Mary, to whom he was engaged and who was expecting a child.” The emperor thinks he is counting his subjects; in fact he is bringing the Son of David to the town where the prophet Micah said the ruler of Israel would be born.

Peter in Acts recalls God's word to Abraham: “In your descendants all the families of the earth shall be blessed” (Acts 3:25). The genealogy does not end with Jesus; it continues in us, the Church, who by Baptism are grafted into this family tree. As Yaldo approaches, we prepare not only to remember a birth, but to welcome the Saviour into our own family history.
conn: Down to Egypt, up to Bethlehem.
Jacob's family went down to Egypt with God's promise: “I myself will go down with you” (Genesis 46:4). Now the Son of God comes down into our history, and his family goes up to Bethlehem.
Isaiah 11:2 describes the Spirit resting on the shoot of Jesse, the source of the gifts of the Spirit.
“The wolf shall live with the lamb” (Isaiah 11:6): the Child of Bethlehem brings a peace that heals even creation.
Hebrews 7:14 notes that our Lord came from Judah, not Levi: a new priesthood “according to the order of Melchizedek”.
altar: Bethlehem means “house of bread”. The Son of David born there gives himself as the Bread of Life. As we go up to Yaldo, each Holy Qurbono is our journey to Bethlehem.
outline: Ask: do you know the names of your great-grandparents? Why do families keep these names?
The genealogies: saints and sinners, Jews and foreigners. Your family history is not outside God's plan.
Point 2 · New life from a stump
Isaiah 11. When something in our life seems cut down, God can make it sprout.
The emperor's decree serves God's plan. God uses even inconvenient events.
The Word that became flesh speaks to us in Scripture. Practical: keep a Bible open at home.
“My family is part of God's story.”
live: Write the names of your grandparents and great-grandparents and pray for them, living and departed.
Read the Christmas Gospel at home
On Christmas Eve, read Luke 2:1–20 together as a family before the crib.
Make your Christmas Confession this week and plan one act of charity for Yaldo.
fathers: Luke traces Christ's genealogy back to Adam to show that Christ “recapitulates” in himself all the nations and generations of humanity, from the beginning (Against Heresies III, 22, 3).
In his Nativity hymns he sings of the Shoot from the root of Jesse, through whom the old trunk of humanity blossoms again (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Jesus was born in a humble stable in Bethlehem; to become a child in relation to God is the condition for entering the kingdom.
Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ (St Jerome); the faithful are urged to frequent reading of the divine Scriptures.
By Baptism we become members of the Body of Christ, the family of God.
saints: 25 Dec (Friday): Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord, Holy Qurbono for the people. 26 Dec: Exaltation of Mary, Mother of God. 27 Dec: Commemoration of the infants killed by Herod (as in the 2025–26 lectionary). Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-12-20.prayer: Lord God, from the stump of Jesse you made a Branch to grow, and through many generations you prepared the birth of your Son. Bless our families and our ancestors, make your Word live in our homes, and lead us like Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, to welcome the Saviour. Amen.

quick: God's salvation comes through real families and real history.
From the cut-down stump of Jesse, God makes new life sprout.
Even Caesar's decree brings Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem.
2026-12-20.action: Read Luke 2:1–20 together as a family on Christmas Eve.
2026-12-20.question: Where in my family history do I need God to make something new sprout?
2026-12-20.special: Sixth Sunday of Suboro, the Sunday before Yaldo (Christmas, Friday 25 December).
illus: At a Kerala family reunion the eldest member reads out the names of the ancestors who brought the faith to the family. The young people discover that their faith has a history. The genealogy of Jesus does the same for the whole Church.

family.explain: Joseph and Mary had to travel a long way to Bethlehem, because the emperor wanted to count everyone. God used that journey so that Jesus would be born in Bethlehem, the town of King David.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and great-grandparents who passed on the faith to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught our family to pray? Let us thank God for them.”

catechism: The angel announces the birth of the Messiah in the city of David.
The Holy Scripture in the life of the Church.
kidsaint: A great scholar who lived in Bethlehem and spent his life translating the Bible so that everyone could read it. He said that not knowing the Scriptures means not knowing Christ. Lesson: read a little of the Bible every day.
term: Syriac for “birth”: the feast of the Nativity of our Lord, 25 December. The season of Yaldo–Denho follows, until the Baptism of the Lord (Denho, 6 January).
termMore: Matthew traces Jesus' line from Abraham through David; Luke traces it back to Adam. Both show that Jesus is the Son of David and the Saviour of all humanity.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, son of David, son of Abraham, you entered our human family through many generations. As we gather on the Sunday before Yaldo, bless our families and our ancestors. Amen.
share: Jesus' genealogy includes saints and sinners (Matthew 1:1–17). What does this tell me about God's love for my family?
Who handed on the faith to me?
How will I prepare my heart in the last days before Yaldo?
pm.resp: Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome Christ with faith at Yaldo.
For our ancestors who handed on the faith.
For families wounded by sin, that Christ may heal them.
For those travelling home for Yaldo.
For our parish, as we complete the Yaldo fast.
pm.close: Lord God, your promises were fulfilled through many generations. Bless our families, heal our history, and make us ready to welcome your Son. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Yaldo, the Church gives us a list of names: the family of Jacob going down to Egypt, and the genealogy of Jesus. Some of us may wonder why. But these names tell us something beautiful: God did not save the world from a distance. He came through a family, generation after generation.

Isaiah uses a picture every farmer in Kerala knows. A tree is cut down; only a stump remains. Then one day a green shoot appears. “A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse.” When the house of David seemed finished, God was preparing the Saviour. When something in our life seems cut down, God can still make it sprout.

Then St Luke tells us how Mary and Joseph came to Bethlehem. Not by their own plan, but because the emperor ordered a census. A very inconvenient journey for a woman expecting a child! Yet God used it so that his Son would be born in the city of David, as the prophet had promised. God can use even the inconvenient events of our lives.

This week, pray for your family tree: for grandparents and great-grandparents who passed on the faith. Make your Christmas Confession. And on Christmas Eve, gather your family and read the Gospel of the Nativity together. Let us go to Bethlehem, the house of bread, to welcome the Saviour. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the names of your grandparents? Jesus had grandparents and great-great-grandparents too! The Bible gives a long list of them, all the way back to Abraham and King David.
Mary and Joseph had to walk a long way to Bethlehem. It was hard, but God had a plan: Jesus would be born in the town of King David.
This Christmas, let's thank God for our family. Let's say together: “Thank you, God, for my family!”

intro: Theme: “The shoot from the stump of Jesse.”

The Sunday before Christmas gives us a long list of names: the genealogy of Jesus. It looks dry, but it tells a great truth: God keeps his promises through real families, with their saints and their sinners, until the Saviour is born.

points.h: God writes salvation through a human family tree
sub: Matthew begins with Abraham and David: God's promise runs through generations.
The list includes sinners and foreigners: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, the wife of Uriah. God's grace works through broken stories.
From a cut-down stump, Isaiah says, a new shoot will grow: no family history is beyond God's hope.
q: A shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
points.apply: Thank God for your family's faith, and pray for its wounds this week.

points.h: A righteous King from David's house
sub: Jeremiah promised a righteous Branch who would do justice.
Joseph, of the house of David, goes to Bethlehem with Mary because of an emperor's decree.
God uses even the plans of the powerful to fulfil his own.
q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal wisely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
Joseph also went from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was descended from the house and family of David.
points.apply: Trust God in the events you cannot control; he is still guiding history.

sub: Isaiah's vision: the wolf and the lamb together, no harm on God's holy mountain.
The angels will sing peace to those whom God favours.
Christmas peace begins in our homes: reconciliation before celebration.
q: They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favors!
points.apply: Before Christmas, make peace with one person and make a good confession.

concl: The long genealogy ends in a manger. God has been faithful through every generation, and he is faithful to us.
Let us prepare our hearts and homes, so that the shoot of Jesse may grow in us.
2026-12-20.resolve: Set up the crib at home this week and pray before it as a family.
